schemaNote: Extends the gold-node-items.json schema conventions (misconceptionMap as {trigger, tag, signature}[] with signatures computed on the item's numbers; acceptedEquivalents where fractional; full visual objects; authoringNote with generator-constraint verification). Battery-specific deltas: batteryDimension field on every item; hintPolicy REPLACES hintLadderRef (battery items are assessment - no ladder is served while the battery runs; wrong answers still log trigger/tag/signature evidence and remediation schedules after the battery resolves); visual may be null ONLY with a visualNote arguing why no spec is needed. Namespace caution (MANIFEST §2): the four battery dimensions are written 'transfer dimension 1-4'; 'D4' elsewhere in gold-node docs names the rubric-contract deliverable.

passRule.statement: A node passes the gate only when it clears all four dimensions at the §3 confidence bound on delayed, unseen items. (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §5, verbatim)
passRule.confidenceBound: lower-bound P(mastery) > 0.90 for prerequisite nodes, 0.85 for leaf nodes (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §3; MUST-VALIDATE - pilot-calibrated, A/B-testable parameter)
passRule.evidencePerDimension: 3-5 successful items per transfer dimension (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §3). The gold items below are the certified exemplar of each dimension's item family; the full battery renders parameter-randomized unseen instances from these families under each item's generator constraints (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §11: randomize numeric parameters per render; novel item families at the gate).
passRule.delayGateNote: Delayed checks at 1, 7, and 21 days; locked mastery is computed ONLY from delayed unseen items - one-sitting accuracy never locks a node (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §2 step 6, §3). AI_ADAPTIVE.md §7 retention firewall: 'Mastery locks only on spaced, delayed, UNSEEN retrieval'; the objective is retained, transferable mastery at delay, never time-to-first-pass.
passRule.unseenRule: Every battery render must be an item instance the student has never seen: numeric parameters re-randomized per render under the item's generator constraints; item families structurally absent from the teaching bank (verified per item in authoringNote against the 62 live ALG-L06 items and the 15 gold-node enriched items); practiced and in-session items feed provisional state only and never count toward the lock (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §3, §11).
passRule.gatingAuthority: The transfer-dimension 1-4 pass decision is deterministic engine logic on the RUNTIME_TUTOR_SPEC §6 never-LLM list (item 4: 'the transfer-battery pass decision across D1-D4'). The rubric-scored explanation element on ALG-L06-gold-tb-d1-01 produces advisory misconception evidence only and never enters the pass computation; that item's closed-form part is its sole gating evidence (RUNTIME §4: provisional state advances only on deterministic evidence; GOLD_NODE_RUBRICS.md §1.2).

items.batteryDimension: transfer dimension 1 (same structure, changed story - foreign domain)
items.prompt: A print shop charges $23.00 for an order of 20 posters and $47.00 for an order of 60 posters. The charge climbs at a steady rate with each added poster. How much does each additional poster add to the charge, in dollars?

misconceptionMap.signature: Δy = 47 - 23 = 24 (dollars) reported as the per-poster rate; Δx never consulted (§2.1; |Δx| = 40 != 1)
Δx/Δy = 40/24 = 5/3 = 1/m: posters-per-dollar where dollars-per-poster was asked (§2.3; |m| = 0.6 != 1); decimal form 1.67 maps to the same tag via the checker's equivalence pass
y1/x1 = 23/20 = 1.15 from one order, ignoring the setup fee b = 11 != 0 (§2.9, armed; separation |1.15 - 0.6| = 0.55 exceeds 2x grading tolerance)
y2/x2 = 47/60 ≈ 0.783 - the §2.9 variant computed at the other point (both variants computed per the entry; separation 0.183 exceeds 2x grading tolerance for exact numeric entry)

visual.purpose: Data vehicle only - an assessment surface, not a scaffold; the two order-size/charge pairs as a table.

data.caption: Two orders from the same price list.

annotations: no per-interval brackets or change labels - the battery assesses unaided transfer
no mid-item reveals; feedback defers to battery review
reveal_beats: Table and prompt appear together; nothing else renders.
(Assessment surface: no reveal on resolve - results surface in the post-battery review.)

items.authoringNote: Transfer dimension 1, foreign domain #2 (>=2 foreign domains satisfied with atmospheric science on tb-d1-01). Structurally fresh, not a reskin: x is ORDER SIZE - a chosen batch size, not a sequential count - so the slope is a unit price ($0.60 per poster over a setup fee), not a pace; the money context differs structurally from the taught savings-over-time neutral item (ALG-L06-p1-neutral-04), whose x is weeks. Realistic dollar values at a tractable path (47 - 23 = 24, 60 - 20 = 40, one division). Generator constraints verified on (20, 23)-(60, 47): |Δx| = 40 != 1, |m| = 0.6 != 1, y1 = 23 != x1 = 20, y1 != 0, b = 11 != 0 (arms §2.9, both variants). Armed traps {24, 5/3, 1.15, 47/60, -16, -13} pairwise distinct and distinct from the key 0.60; accepted equivalents collision-checked against all traps (no matches). Unseen verified: live ALG-L06 x-variables do include event counts (plate appearances, fouls committed, play number) - all sequential counts; what is absent, live and gold, is an order-size/unit-price construct - no item prices a batch against a setup fee.

dimension2.definition: Changed representation, same structure - table <-> graph <-> equation <-> word <-> verbal. (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §5.2; the §5 note: this dimension IS representation transfer - fluent mapping across representations, not bare symbolic)
dimension2.coverageNote: Per-node GENERATED batteries require >=2 distinct representation pairings for dimension 2 (drawn from table <-> graph <-> equation <-> word <-> verbal). The single gold graph -> table family below is the pattern exemplar, not the coverage standard.

items.representationPairing: graph -> table (unseen pairing; teaching had table -> graph construction and graph -> numeric reads, never graph -> table matching)
items.prompt: The graph shows a line through the labeled points (1, 25) and (3, 55). Which table climbs at the same rate as this line?

misconceptionMap.signature: table rate 3 = m*(s_x/s_y) = 15*(1/5): the line rises 3 gridsquares per square right, and squares were never converted to axis units (§2.11; armed because s_x = 1 != s_y = 5). §2.11's severity note says this error is invisible on equal-scale teaching graphs and detonates in the transfer battery's representation dimension - this item is that detonation point, authored deliberately
table rate 30 = Δy = 55 - 25: the change between the labeled points taken as the per-step rate (§2.1; |Δx| = 2 != 1)
table rate 55 = y2: the height of the line at the right labeled point read as its rate (§2.8; y1 = 25 != 0 so y2 != Δy, and y2 = 55 != m = 15)

visual.purpose: Deliberately unequal axis scales (§2.11's authoring mandate at the gate): square-counting and axis-reading give different rates on the same picture, and only the axis-read rate matches a choice correctly.

data.line: solid through both points, extended across the plot (y = 15x + 10)

annotations: every y-axis tick label (0, 5, 10, ... 60) rendered - the scale is fully available; consulting it is the assessed behavior
choice tables render beside the plane; no rate readouts anywhere before resolve
reveal_beats: Plane with unequal scales, both labeled points, the line, and the four candidate tables appear; student answers.
(Assessment surface: no reveal on resolve - results surface in the post-battery review.)

items.authoringNote: Transfer dimension 2 with the unseen pairing graph -> table: teaching covered table -> graph construction (int-03) and graph -> numeric slope reads (disc-02, pr-01), never matching a graphed line to a table by rate. Assessment-register MC: exactly 3 distractors, each produced by a named taxonomy error path (rates 3, 30, 55 vs key rate 15 - pairwise distinct). All four tables share start value 10 so ONLY the rate discriminates. Line y = 15x + 10 puts both labeled points and the intercept on gridline intersections (25 = 5 squares, 55 = 11 squares). Generator constraints verified: s_x = 1 != s_y = 5 (arms §2.11), |Δx| = 2 != 1 (§2.1 live), y1 = 25 != 0 and y2 = 55 != m (arms §2.8), m = 15 (|m| != 1). Clean values by construct: gridline alignment requires them (construct-integrity exemption, MANIFEST §5).

items.prompt: Two points on a line are recorded as x₁ = 4, y₁ = 21, x₂ = 10, and y₂ = 6. What is the slope m of the line?

misconceptionMap.signature: -m = |m| = 5/2 since m = -5/2 < 0: ambiguous between §2.2 and §2.5 - log the pair, tag neither active, queue a positive-slope probe per the collision matrix

(y₂ - x₂)/(y₁ - x₁) = (6 - 10)/(21 - 4) = -4/17: differences formed inside each subscript group instead of across points (§2.7; y1 = 21 != x1 = 4). The subscript-assignment surface is exactly where §2.7's '2-stuff over the 1-stuff' parsing lives - this item is its sharpest probe

items.visualNote: Deliberately none (argued, per the no-nulls convention): transfer dimension 3 assesses the decontextualized symbolic form; a plane or table would reintroduce exactly the representation support this dimension exists to remove. The lesson §6 subscript notation (x₁, y₁, x₂, y₂ as 'name tags') is the item's entire surface.
items.hintPolicyNote: Assessment item: no hint ladder during the battery; taxonomy evidence still logs and remediation schedules after the battery resolves.
items.authoringNote: Transfer dimension 3 in the lesson §6 notation. Structurally fresh: every teaching item (live and gold) presents coordinates as ordered pairs '(4, 21)'; here they arrive as four separated subscript assignments, so the student must bind each subscript to its role before any arithmetic - unseen surface, same structure. Generator constraints verified on x₁=4, y₁=21, x₂=10, y₂=6: |Δx| = 6 != 1, |m| = 5/2 != 1, y1 = 21 != x1 = 4 (§2.6 variants and §2.7 denominators live), y1 != 0. Armed traps {-15, 5/2, -2/5, -4/17, -21, -4} pairwise distinct and distinct from the key -5/2; accepted equivalents (-2.5, -15/6) collision-checked against all traps (no matches). Negative fraction slope keeps the §2.2/§2.5 ambiguity honest at the gate (pair logged, probe queued, per the matrix).

dimension4.definition: Novel problem form - a question shape not seen during teaching. (new_plan/CLAUDE.md §5.4)

items.novelForm: inverse: slope and one point given, a second point's y-coordinate given - find its x-coordinate (the slope relation run backward, solving for the input)
items.prompt: A line has a slope of 5 and passes through the point (4, 7). The line also passes through a second point with y-coordinate 42. What is the x-coordinate of that second point?

misconceptionMap.signature: x = y/m = 42/5 = 8.4: believes every point satisfies y/x = m, solving 42/x = 5 (§2.9; armed because b = 7 - 5*4 = -13 != 0; separation |8.4 - 11| = 2.6 exceeds 2x grading tolerance)
believes m = Δx/Δy, so Δx = 5 * 35 = 175 and x = 4 + 175 = 179 - the §2.3 inversion run through the inverse form (|m| = 5 != 1)
believes slope compares the changes by subtraction: 5 = 35 - Δx gives Δx = 30 and x = 4 + 30 = 34 - §2.6 solved inversely (y1 = 7 != x1 = 4)

items.visualNote: Deliberately none (argued, per the no-nulls convention): the novel form asks the student to run the slope relation backward from the symbolic statement alone. Plotting the line with the target height y = 42 would let rise and run be read off the picture, collapsing the inverse move into a forward graph-read and voiding the dimension.
items.hintPolicyNote: Assessment item: no hint ladder during the battery; taxonomy evidence still logs and remediation schedules after the battery resolves.
items.authoringNote: Transfer dimension 4. Novel-form verification against the full teaching bank: all 62 live ALG-L06 items are forward two-point slope computations; the gold bank's only coordinate-finding part (scaf-03 part (b)) is forward (x given, find y, slope self-computed from part (a)). No item anywhere gives m and asks for a missing coordinate, and solving for the INPUT coordinate x is doubly absent - the question shape is unseen. Correct path: Δy = 42 - 7 = 35; Δx = Δy/m = 35/5 = 7; x = 4 + 7 = 11. Generator constraints verified: |m| = 5 != 1 (else the §2.3 inverse trap collapses onto the key), Δx = 7 != 1, Δy/m integral (keeps the inverse path clean by construct), b = -13 != 0 (arms §2.9). Armed traps {8.4, 179, 34} pairwise distinct and distinct from the key 11. The bare answer '7' (Δx typed instead of the coordinate) is a slip, not a taxonomy belief: it logs misconception_tag null per §2.15 and feeds the taxonomy-growth loop.
